title: The First Echo
logline: The grove repeats the egg a beat late — so there always seems to be a second one just out of sight.
epigraph: Repetition is not proof. It is only pressure.
description: Chapter 2 of Lore.Land: The First Echo. Boof carries the unnamed egg into the grove that answers a beat late, where pollen grains sleep and wake, and an echo is not a receipt.

content.text: By the second morning the egg was warmer than the sling, and the sling was warmer than Boof, and the maps were still pretending none of this was a fact. She had walked downhill the way the berries pointed, off the edge of every route she carried, into the treeline the workers would not name after dark. The grove smelled of wet bark and of something arriving twice.

She set the egg on a stone at the clearing's rim and watched the air around it thicken. Pollen hung in ring after ring. A spoken breath left her muzzle and came back a heartbeat later, wearing her own pitch, as if the thicket had kept a grain of the sound asleep and then woken it. The egg did not echo. The grove echoed the egg.

content.text: The berries here did not shine for distribution. They shone like grains under stress—bright when a phrase repeated often enough to become policy, dim when the thicket put them back to sleep. Boof recognized several of her own silences reflected in the fruit. That was the grove’s first cruelty: it kept what the town preferred not to receipt.

content.text: "Follow me," said an echo that used Boof’s own pitch from years earlier, the careful clerk-voice that had once made disorder sound administrative. The path forked and rejoined. Time did not reverse; it re-litigated. In the hanging dust there was always a second egg, a breath behind the first, as if the grove were practicing a clutch it did not yet have the right to keep.

sections.figcaption: The Grove of Echoes: an echo is a summons, not a receipt.

content.text: Boof understood, pacing the fork, that the grove was not a memory palace. It was a failure mode of the archive—overflow storage for stories that had been published too cleanly. Each echo offered a route: amplify a grievance, bury a name, promote a rumor until it calcified into map legend. None of those routes would issue a receipt for the egg. The grove could repeat it. It could not file it.

Choosing a path was authorship. Leaving without choosing was also authorship, only quieter, and the grove charged interest on quiet. Boof took the egg back into the sling. The second egg in the pollen stayed where it was, a witness the thicket would not swear to. Down-sand, older routes had begun to answer. She went to hear which of them would admit a turn.
"Are you lost?" the Fool asked from nowhere particular, no longer playful. "Or have you finally arrived where the public record cannot pretend to be complete?"

Boof did not answer with a riddle. She opened no book. She wrote the grove’s first usable note on the air with her nose: echo is not evidence; echo is a summons; a summons is not a receipt. Then she kept walking, because a summons still requires a response if anyone is to stay warm.

loreItems.description: Boof is a dog guide; echoes are old scents re-lit, not automatic proof.
The Grove of Echoes retains overflow testimony the polished archive will not receipt.
Pollen grains in the grove sleep and wake. Brightness is not policy until someone files it.
The grove repeats the egg a beat late, so there always seems to be a second one just out of sight.
An echo is a summons, not a receipt. Boof records this and continues toward the sand.
